question: Which part of the abdomen is the spleen normally found in?
explanation: The spleen sits tucked under the diaphragm on the left side of the upper abdomen. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why is a healthy spleen usually not felt during a routine belly check?

options.A: It is too small to ever be touched by human hands
options.B: It floats freely in the middle of the abdominal cavity
options.C: It is hidden behind the lower ribs and diaphragm
options.D: It is completely covered by a thick layer of bone

explanation: Because the normal spleen is tucked up high under the ribcage, you cannot feel it by pressing on the belly unless it is enlarged. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which part of the spleen is mainly responsible for fighting infections?
explanation: The white pulp contains special immune cells that help the body fight off germs found in the blood. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h2)

question: What fills the red pulp of the spleen?
explanation: The red pulp gets its color and function from a network of small blood vessels and circulating blood cells. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h2)

question: What happens to the iron salvaged from old red blood cells inside the spleen?

options.A: It is converted into waste products by local macrophages
options.B: It is transported back to the bone marrow to make new cells
options.C: It is stored permanently inside the splenic capsule
options.D: It is excreted immediately through the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: The spleen saves iron from worn-out blood cells and sends it back to the bone marrow to help create new ones. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h3)

question: Which cells in the spleen break down worn-out blood cells?
explanation: Special cleanup cells called macrophages patrol the spleen to clear out old or damaged blood cells. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h3)

question: Against which type of germ does the spleen provide especially important defense?
explanation: The spleen is uniquely equipped to filter out specific types of bacteria with protective outer coats from the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h4)

question: A patient loses their spleen in an accident. What health step is most important for them afterward?

options.A: Undergoing weekly blood transfusions to maintain volume
options.B: Receiving specific vaccinations against bacterial infections
options.C: Taking daily high-dose iron supplements to replace lost stores
options.D: Avoiding all physical exercise to prevent internal bleeding

explanation: Without a spleen, patients lose their primary defense against certain bacteria, making targeted vaccinations vital. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h4)

question: About how many of the body's total platelets are stored in a normal spleen?
explanation: The spleen keeps about one-third of the body's platelets in reserve, ready to be released if bleeding happens. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h5)

question: When might an adult spleen start producing blood cells again?

options.A: Right after eating a large meal high in dietary iron
options.B: During normal, healthy adult physical exercise
options.C: Whenever a person donates whole blood at a clinic
options.D: When severe bone marrow disease or failure occurs

explanation: While blood cell production normally happens in the bone marrow after birth, the spleen can restart production if the bone marrow stops working properly. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h5)

question: What is the main danger of a ruptured spleen caused by an injury?

options.A: Instant paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Permanent loss of digestive enzyme secretion

explanation: The spleen holds a large amount of blood, so a severe tear leads to rapid internal bleeding that can quickly cause shock. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h6)

question: Why must midwives teach patients who have had their spleen removed to watch out for early signs of infection?

options.A: Their blood pressure will drop dangerously every morning
options.B: They will produce excess platelets that cause frequent clots
options.C: Their bodies lose a major filter against severe bacterial infections
options.D: They will permanently lose the ability to digest dietary proteins

explanation: Removing the spleen lowers the body's ability to filter out certain bacteria, making it essential to catch and treat fevers early. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h6)
